composition_label: Sentiment & prioritization -> Deep research -> Interest-based recommendations

construction.implementation_origin: Written from scratch for this isolated construction using synthetic fixtures.

shared_schema.definition: SCHEMAS in implementation.py; one validate() layer checks exact shape, types, constraints and deterministic derivation/provenance at every handoff.

input.fixture_label: Nonblank label; the example explicitly identifies synthetic data.
input.feedback: Array of {id, topic, text, severity}; severity is low|medium|high|critical.
input.documents: Array of {id,title,text,evidence:[{topic,claim,stance,quote}]}; stance is support|refute|uncertain. quote must be an exact substring of document text.
input.catalog: Array of {id,title,tags:[string],topics:[string]}; tag and topic joins are exact and case-sensitive.

shared_schema.output: One object: {status:ok,schema_version,fixture_label,sentiment:{issues},research:{topics},recommendations:{ranked,excluded_item_ids}}. Each stage exposes structured provenance.
shared_schema.errors: File, decoding, JSON and validation errors emit one {status:error,error:string} object to stdout and exit 2; success exits 0.
shared_schema.bounds: Each array at most 1000 entries; nonblank strings at most 100000 characters; CLI input file at most 2000000 bytes. Duplicate IDs, repeated interests/tags and exact duplicate evidence within a document are rejected. Missing and unknown object fields are rejected.
shared_schema.empty_policy: Empty collections accepted. No feedback yields no research topics; missing evidence yields unresolved questions and no recommendations for that topic. No interests, no eligible matches, or limit 0 yields an empty ranking.
shared_schema.identifiers: IDs unique within their entity collection. Unknown exclusion IDs are permitted for forward-compatible blocking. Documents and catalog topics outside feedback are allowed but cannot produce research or recommendations.

cross_stage_handoffs.contract: Validated issues carry ID, topic, severity, score, label, token contributions and priority. Research groups only these issues, preserves ordered issue IDs, inherits maximum priority and counts negative issues.

Validated research carries topics, priorities, issue IDs, document IDs, findings with verbatim evidence, disagreement and unresolved questions. Recommendations require both an interest match and a researched topic with evidence; carry issue/document IDs and uncertainty cautions.

behavior.sentiment: Lowercase ASCII word lexicon with exposed weights and contributions; odd count of not/never/no within preceding three words negates a match, punctuation resets scope. Sum clipped to [-10,10]. Priority is severity base (10,30,60,90) plus max(0,-score). Sort descending priority then ID.
behavior.research: Group structured claims by exact topic and claim string across documents, with no inferred semantic equivalence. Opposed stances mark contested; uncertain stance prevents consensus. Single-document claims request corroboration. Unsupported topics, disagreement and uncertainty produce unresolved questions. Quotes are retained verbatim; status represents supplied annotations, not independently verified truth.
behavior.recommendations: Exclude by item ID or any excluded tag before ranking. Require a preferred tag and a topic with research findings. Score = 100 * sum matched interest weights + floor(max matched topic priority / 2). Research bonus is at most 50, so a unit of expressed interest dominates. Rank descending score then item ID; truncate only after exclusions. Explanations cite interests, topics, issues and documents; propagate unresolved questions and refuted-claim cautions. A match indicates topical relevance, not item effectiveness.
behavior.determinism: No randomness, clocks, network calls or model providers in the pipeline; stable tie-breaks and sorted evidence.
behavior.fixture: All example customer feedback, research and catalog entries are fictional synthetic data.

included: Integrated three-stage pipeline with strict validated boundaries
Transparent rule-based sentiment and severity prioritization
Multi-document structured evidence synthesis and provenance
Conflicts, evidence gaps, uncertainty and corroboration questions
Explicit preference ranking and hard exclusions
Runnable CLI and standard-library unittest coverage
excluded: Live research, web scraping, provider or LLM calls
Semantic claim extraction, embeddings and learned sentiment
Independent source authenticity or factuality verification
Sarcasm, multilingual sentiment and full natural-language negation parsing
Production scalability, databases, user identity and enterprise delivery

test_outcomes.cli_output: One valid JSON object with status ok; two grounded recommendations and two enforced catalog exclusions.
test_outcomes.coverage: All three stages, sentiment scoring/negation/clamping, severity, multi-document agreement and conflict, uncertainty and missing evidence, provenance, preference ranking/exclusions, both validated handoffs, forged intermediate/output rejection, empty inputs, determinism, strict invalid-input handling, subprocess CLI success/file/usage errors and fixture-injected parsing/decoding errors.
